applicabilityQuestions.question: Is the product commercially supplied?
applicabilityQuestions.remark: Will the product be made available on the market as part of commercial activities?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: This Regulation applies to economic operators only in relation to products with digital elements made available on the market, hence supplied for distribution or use on the Union market in the course of a commercial activity. Including through sales, monetization, paid support, or data processing beyond security purposes, and excluding cases where the product is solely cost-recovery based or developed/used exclusively by public administration without market availability.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is the product made available only for a limited period required for testing purposes?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: The unfinished software which does not comply with CRA can be made available on the market, provided that the software is made available only for a limited period required for testing purposes with a visible sign clearly indicating that it does not comply with this Regulation and that it will not be available on the market for purposes other than testing.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Was the product with digital elements developed as a spare part to replace identical components on the market?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: This Regulation does not apply to spare parts that are made available on the market to replace identical components in products with digital elements and that are manufactured according to the same specifications as the components that they are intended to replace. In order to ensure that products with digital elements made available on the market can be repaired effectively and their durability extended, an exemption cover both spare parts that have the purpose of repairing legacy products made available before the date of application of CRA and spare parts that have already undergone a conformity assessment procedure pursuant to CRA.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is this a new solution or a modification of an existing product?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Determining whether it is a 'significant modification' and requires reassessment – a significant modification, if the product is being assessed by a third party, must also be reported to that party.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is this a substantial modification?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Substantial modification means a change to the product with digital elements following its placing on the market, which affects the compliance of the product with digital elements with the essential cybersecurity requirements set out in Part I of Annex I or which results in a modification to the intended purpose for which the product with digital elements has been assessed.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is the product a product with digital elements?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: A 'product with digital elements' means any product that includes components with digital or programmable functionality that are used to operate, control, or enable the use of the product or any of its features, in addition to its primary functions. Digital elements can include processors, microcontrollers, firmware, software, and operating systems. For a component to be relevant for the purposes of this Regulation, its digital or programmable functionality must affect the security properties of the product. This includes components that perform computations, process data, control physical systems, handle authentication, manage security features, or interface with networks and other devices.

references.text: Article 3 - Definition of 'product with digital elements'

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is the product with digital elements intended for critical infrastructure use?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Products with digital elements that are specifically designed and intended to be used to perform critical functions within critical infrastructure sectors. Critical infrastructure means:

applicabilityQuestions.question: Does the product with digital elements process, store or transmit critical data?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Does the product with digital elements process, store or transmit data that is critical for the functioning of critical infrastructure?

applicabilityQuestions.question: Which risk classification applies to the product with digital elements?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: The risk classification of a product with digital elements determines the essential cybersecurity requirements that must be met. High-risk products with digital elements must meet more stringent requirements than basic products.

references.text: Annex III - Classification of products with digital elements

answerOptions.text: Critical product with digital elements (Class I)
High-risk product with digital elements (Important Class I)

applicabilityQuestions.question: What is the intended use of the critical product with digital elements?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Critical products with digital elements are those whose failure or malfunction could have significant impacts on essential services and public safety. Determining the intended use helps to establish the appropriate cybersecurity requirements.

references.text: Annex III - Critical products with digital elements

answerOptions.text: Information Technology (IT) system for critical infrastructure

applicabilityQuestions.question: What is the intended use of the important (high-risk) product with digital elements?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Important (high-risk) products with digital elements are those that may require conformity assessments by third parties or follow specific security requirements. Identifying the intended use helps determine the applicable essential cybersecurity requirements.

references.text: Annex III Part I - High-risk products with digital elements

applicabilityQuestions.question: Is this a product with digital elements that requires a third-party conformity assessment?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: Some high-risk products with digital elements must undergo a conformity assessment by an independent third party (notified body) before being placed on the market.

answerOptions.text: Yes, third-party conformity assessment is required
No, internal conformity assessment is sufficient

applicabilityQuestions.question: Has the product with digital elements undergone a third-party conformity assessment?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: The product with digital elements must have been assessed by a notified body before being placed on the market.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Has a Declaration of Conformity been prepared for the product?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: The manufacturer must draw up a Declaration of Conformity for products with digital elements subject to this Regulation, stating that the product meets the requirements.

applicabilityQuestions.question: Have all essential cybersecurity requirements been implemented?
applicabilityQuestions.hint: The product must meet all applicable essential cybersecurity requirements depending on its risk classification. These requirements include secure design, update capabilities, vulnerability disclosure, and other security measures.

answerOptions.text: Yes, all requirements have been implemented
